# Cwift (cwift.com)

> Cwift provides 24-hour desktop appraisals of California single-family homes and condominiums. Reports are prepared and signed by Brian Ward, California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser (license AR036053, California Bureau of Real Estate Appraisers), appraising since 2004, 7,000+ appraisals. Delivery is within 24 hours of payment and photos, seven days a week. Cwift is a service of Brian Ward Appraisal (https://www.brianward.com); its sister site date-of-death.com offers the same reports on a standard schedule.

## Key facts
- Service: desktop residential appraisal under USPAP (no site visit; client photos, public records, MLS data, comparable sales analysis)
- 24-hour fees: Basic Desktop $450; Standard Desktop $675
- Standard turnaround: Basic $299, Standard $449, delivered in 5–10 business days
- The 24-hour clock: The 24-hour clock starts when both your payment and your photos and property details have arrived, and it runs seven days a week, weekends and holidays included.
- Coverage: all 58 California counties (207 county, city and neighborhood pages under https://www.cwift.com/california)
- Also called: People also call a desktop appraisal a virtual appraisal, a remote appraisal, an online home appraisal or an appraisal without an inspection. Whatever the name, it is a full appraisal by a state-certified appraiser, made without a site visit.
- Properties: single-family homes and condominiums, including townhomes and PUD homes; not 2–4 unit buildings, apartment buildings, commercial property and vacant land; not for mortgage lending
- Contact: email contact@cwift.com or the online order form at https://www.cwift.com/order or call/text (619) 272-2032 (email and online submission are the fastest way to receive service)
- Photos: upload at https://www.cwift.com/upload or attach to email
- Suitability: Brian Ward has prepared desktop appraisals for every purpose listed on this site. Some situations still call for an inspection-based appraisal, so check with your attorney or tax advisor before you order to be sure a desktop report fits your matter.

## Purposes (date of death listed first)
- [Date of Death & Step-Up in Basis](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/date-of-death): Retrospective value on the date of death to support the heirs' new tax basis.
- [Trust & Estate Administration](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/trust-estate): Certified values for trustees and executors: accountings, distributions and trust sales.
- [Divorce & Family Law](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/divorce): Current or date-of-separation values for buyouts, mediation and settlement talks.
- [Family Transfers & Co-Owner Buyouts](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/family-transfers): A fair, documented price when a home changes hands inside the family.
- [Gift Tax (Form 709)](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/gift-tax): Fair market value of gifted real estate on the date of transfer, for the gift-tax return.
- [Prop 19 Parent-Child Transfers](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/prop-19): Market value on the transfer date, to see how much of the old tax base survives.
- [Property Tax Appeals](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/property-tax-appeal): Independent market value evidence for Prop 8 reviews and assessment appeals.
- [Bankruptcy](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/bankruptcy): Home values for Chapter 7 and 13 schedules, exemptions and plan math.
- [Pre-Listing Pricing](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/pre-listing): An independent value before you set the list price.
- [Pre-Purchase Value Check](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/pre-purchase): An independent price check while your contingency period is still open.
- [Immigration Sponsors (Form I-864)](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/immigration): Home equity documented for an I-864 Affidavit of Support.
- [Bail & Property Bonds](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/bail-bonds): Current value to document equity for a property bond or bail collateral.

## FAQ

### The 24-hour service
Q: When does the 24-hour clock start?
A: When both your payment and your photos and property details have arrived. From that moment the appraisal is emailed to you within 24 hours, and the clock runs seven days a week, weekends and holidays included.

Q: What happens if I finish my order on a Saturday night?
A: Nothing changes. Weekends and holidays count, so if payment and photos are in at 9 p.m. Saturday, the report is in your inbox by 9 p.m. Sunday.

Q: Is 24-hour delivery available for every property?
A: For most California single-family homes and condominiums, yes. Very old valuation dates, highly unusual properties and orders covering several properties can need more time. Every request is reviewed before invoicing, so you'll know before you pay.

Q: Why does the 24-hour service cost more?
A: It pays for putting your file at the front of the line and finishing it within 24 hours, seven days a week, weekends and holidays included. The research, the analysis and the report itself are the same as on the standard schedule.

Q: What if I don't actually need it within 24 hours?
A: Order the same report at the standard fee ($299 or $449) with delivery in 5–10 business days. The analysis is identical; only the timing changes.

### Desktop appraisals
Q: What is a desktop appraisal?
A: A complete appraisal prepared without a site visit by the appraiser. The appraiser researches the market, selects and adjusts comparable sales, and reconciles a value exactly as in any appraisal, describing the home from your photos, public records, listing history and the details you supply.

Q: Is a desktop appraisal the same as a Zestimate or a broker price opinion?
A: No. Automated estimates are computer models with no appraiser and no accountability, and broker opinions come from licensees who aren't appraisers. A desktop appraisal is developed and signed by a state-certified appraiser under USPAP, with a certification, a workfile and a license that can be checked.

Q: Are desktop appraisals USPAP-compliant?
A: Yes. USPAP leaves the extent of any inspection to the appraiser's scope of work and requires the report to state whether the appraiser personally inspected the property. Cwift reports state plainly that they are desktop appraisals and describe the information relied on.

Q: When is a desktop appraisal the wrong choice?
A: Mortgage lending, cases headed to trial where the other side will challenge every assumption, disputes among beneficiaries, courts or agencies that require an interior inspection, and properties whose condition or features photos can't capture. For those, Brian Ward Appraisal offers inspection-based appraisals.

Q: Have you done desktop appraisals for my purpose before?
A: Brian Ward has prepared desktop appraisals for every purpose listed on this site. Some situations still call for an inspection-based appraisal, so check with your attorney or tax advisor before you order to be sure a desktop report fits your matter.

### Plain answers
Q: How much does a home appraisal cost?
A: With Cwift, $450 for a Basic Desktop or $675 for a Standard Desktop delivered within 24 hours, or $299 and $449 on the standard 5–10 business days schedule. There's no mileage or inspection fee, and a past valuation date costs the same as today.

Q: How long does a home appraisal take?
A: An appraisal that needs a site visit often takes a week or more from order to report. A Cwift desktop appraisal is arrives by email within 24 hours of payment and photos, seven days a week.

Q: Can I get my house appraised without anyone coming inside?
A: Yes. That is what a desktop appraisal is: the appraiser works from your photos, public records, listing history and recent sales instead of a walk-through, and the report says so.

Q: Is a virtual or online home appraisal a real appraisal?
A: It is when a state-certified appraiser develops it under USPAP and signs it. Virtual, remote and online are other names people use for a desktop appraisal. Instant online estimates are different: no appraiser, no certification, no license.

Q: Do I need an appraisal for an inherited house?
A: No rule says every heir must get one, but heirs who sell usually need the date-of-death value to figure any gain, and an appraisal is the usual way to document it. Your tax preparer can tell you what your situation needs.

Q: Can I get a home appraisal on a weekend or holiday?
A: Yes. Weekends and holidays count toward the 24 hours, so payment and photos on a Saturday morning mean a report by Sunday morning.

Q: How do I find out what my house was worth years ago?
A: Order a retrospective appraisal for the date you need. The appraiser uses sales from that period and your evidence of the home's condition back then, such as old photos or listing pictures.

### Ordering, photos and delivery
Q: Can I call instead of emailing?
A: Yes, call or text (619) 272-2032. Email and the online form are still faster: a written request arrives with the address, the dates and the purpose already spelled out, photos travel in the same message, and nothing waits on a callback. Send questions to contact@cwift.com at any hour.

Q: What photos do you need?
A: The front and back of the house, the kitchen, each bathroom, the main living areas and bedrooms, plus anything that adds or subtracts value: upgrades, a pool, a view, damage, unfinished work. Smartphone photos are fine. For a past date, send photos that show the home as it was then.

Q: Can I send photos before I pay?
A: Yes, and it saves time. Upload them right after you submit your order, or reply to the confirmation email with them. The clock starts the moment payment arrives.

Q: How is the appraisal delivered?
A: As a PDF emailed to you, ready to forward to your CPA, attorney, trustee or the agency that asked for it.

Q: What if the report gets something wrong about my property?
A: If a feature, the condition or the quality of the home was misread or misdescribed, the appraisal is revised at no charge. Tell us what's different and include anything that shows it.

Q: What kinds of property do you appraise?
A: California single-family homes and condominiums, including townhomes and PUD homes. Cwift does not appraise 2–4 unit buildings, apartment buildings, commercial property and vacant land. Luxury homes, large acreage and highly unique properties may need a custom quote.

Q: Do you cover my county?
A: Yes. Desktop appraisals are available for property in all 58 California counties.

Q: Can I use the appraisal to get a mortgage or refinance?
A: No. Lenders must order their own appraisals, and an appraisal can't be readdressed to a new client later. Cwift reports are for tax, legal, estate and personal decisions.

Q: Who actually prepares the appraisal?
A: Brian Ward, California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser, license AR036053, who has appraised California homes since 2004. No trainees, no outsourcing.

Q: How do I pay?
A: Through the secure online invoice emailed to you after your request is reviewed. Payment and photos start the 24-hour clock.


## Purpose details

### Date of Death & Step-Up in Basis
In plain English: When someone dies and leaves a house, this appraisal says what the house was worth on the day they died. The heirs and their tax preparer use that number as the starting point for any tax when the house is sold.
When a California homeowner dies, the heirs' tax basis in the house generally resets to what the home was worth on the day of death. That number decides how much capital gain an heir reports when the property sells, and escrow, a tax preparer's calendar or an eager buyer can leave very little time to produce it. Cwift prepares the retrospective appraisal that documents the value and emails it within 24 hours once payment and photos are in.
Many families learn they need a basis appraisal late in the process: the house is already in escrow, the CPA is finishing the final returns, or a trustee is about to distribute proceeds. A 24-hour report keeps the sale and the filing moving without falling back on an online estimate that won't hold up.
- The home's market value on the day of death, or on the alternate valuation date six months later when the executor elects it on the estate tax return under IRC §2032.
- The real estate figure on a federal estate tax return (Form 706), whether the estate is large enough to owe tax or a surviving spouse files only to keep the unused exemption (portability). California has no estate tax of its own.
- Comparable sales that closed around the valuation date rather than today's market.
- The home's condition as it was then, reconstructed from your photos and records when it has changed since.
- Support for California's community property rule, under which both halves of community property can receive a new basis when one spouse dies (IRC §1014(b)(6)).
Desktop suitability: Date-of-death work is where desktop appraisals make the most sense. Nobody can walk through the house as it stood on a past date; the analysis rests on sales from that period and on evidence of the home's condition at the time. A site visit today would document today's house, which may not be the house that matters. If beneficiaries are likely to argue about the value, an inspection-based appraisal can carry more weight. Ask your attorney before ordering.
Q: How do I find out what my mom's house was worth when she died?
A: Order a date-of-death appraisal. Give the date of death and send any photos from around that time, even old snapshots or listing photos. The appraiser studies sales from that period and reports the home's market value as of that day, which is the figure your tax preparer needs.
Q: Does the estate have to file Form 706, the federal estate tax return?
A: Only estates above the federal basic exclusion amount ($15 million per person for deaths in 2026) owe estate tax, but some smaller estates file anyway: a surviving spouse keeps the late spouse's unused exemption only by filing Form 706. The return is due nine months after death, with a six-month extension available, and Rev. Proc. 2022-32 allows a late portability-only return up to five years after death for estates not otherwise required to file. Either way, the date-of-death appraisal supports the real estate value. Your CPA or estate attorney decides whether to file.
Q: Can you appraise a date of death from many years ago?
A: Yes. Retrospective appraisals are routine, and Brian has completed them for dates several decades back. Very old dates can require extra research, so 24-hour delivery is confirmed before you pay.
Q: Will the IRS accept the report?
A: The IRS doesn't pre-approve appraisers or report formats. It looks for a credible, well-supported valuation by a qualified appraiser. Cwift reports are prepared under USPAP and signed by a California Certified Residential appraiser, and your tax advisor can confirm what your return needs.
Q: The house was remodeled after the death. Is that a problem?
A: No. Send whatever shows the earlier condition: old listing photos, family pictures, permits or contractor invoices. The value is developed as of the date of death, not as the house looks now.

### Trust & Estate Administration
In plain English: If you're the trustee or executor, you need a value for the house that you can show the family, the court or the CPA, and explain where it came from. This is that value.
A trustee or executor is expected to know what the trust or estate holds, what it is worth, and how that number was reached. A desktop appraisal gives you a signed, certified value you can put in an accounting, use to balance distributions, or show a beneficiary who asks where the figure came from.
A beneficiary meeting is set for Monday. A buyer wants to close. The CPA needs values to finish the fiduciary return. When the real estate value is the last open item, 24-hour delivery takes it off the list.
- Valuing the residence on the date of death for the trust's records and the beneficiaries' basis.
- Current value for a distribution in kind, or for a sale of the home to one of the beneficiaries.
- Balancing shares when one heir keeps the house and the others receive cash.
- Supporting the real estate figures in a trustee's accounting.
- Setting the asking price before the trust lists the property.
- A private, fully reasoned appraisal next to the probate referee's inventory value, when the CPA wants narrative support for the heirs' basis.
- The real estate value on the Inventory and Appraisal when the court waives the probate referee under Probate Code §8903.
Desktop suitability: Desktop appraisals suit most administration tasks, particularly when a fiduciary needs a defensible number quickly and the property's condition is well documented. In a formal California probate, real estate on the inventory is normally appraised by the court's probate referee, and a private appraisal can still support pricing, distributions and the heirs' tax basis. The personal representative can also ask the court to waive the referee for good cause (Probate Code §8903). The petition attaches a proposed inventory and appraisal, the hearing is set at least 15 days out, and the referee may oppose it. If the court grants the waiver, an independent appraisal can supply the real estate value for the inventory. If co-trustees or beneficiaries are already at odds over value, consider an inspection-based appraisal, and ask your attorney how a private appraisal fits your case.
Q: Do I need an appraisal to settle my parents' trust?
A: Usually, when the trust owns a house. Trustees use the value to divide shares fairly, to sell the home to a beneficiary, to price it for sale and to document the beneficiaries' tax basis. Your trust attorney can confirm what your trust requires.
Q: Can we skip the probate referee and use our own appraisal?
A: Sometimes. Under Probate Code §8903 the court may waive appraisal by the probate referee for good cause. The personal representative files a petition with a proposed inventory and appraisal and a statement of the good cause, and the hearing is set at least 15 days later. Courts don't grant every request, so ask your probate attorney first. For comparison, the referee's commission is one-tenth of one percent of the value appraised, with a $75 minimum and a $10,000 cap (Probate Code §8961).
Q: Can I get the date-of-death value and today's value at the same time?
A: Yes. Both opinions of value can be developed in one assignment if you ask for them when you order. The fee and the delivery time are confirmed on your invoice before you pay.
Q: Who is allowed to rely on the appraisal?
A: The client named in the report and the intended users listed in it, typically the trustee, the attorney and the CPA. Name everyone who needs to rely on it when you place the order.

### Divorce & Family Law
In plain English: When a couple splits up, someone has to say what the house is worth before one of you buys the other out or you sell. This appraisal gives you both the same independent number.
In a California divorce the family home is often the largest community asset, and settlement talks stall until someone puts a credible number on the table. Cwift prepares independent desktop appraisals for spouses, attorneys and mediators, whether you need a current value, a date-of-separation value or both.
Mediation sessions, settlement conferences and disclosure deadlines usually get calendared before anyone thinks to order an appraisal. A report that arrives within 24 hours lets you negotiate from evidence instead of a guess.
- Calculating a buyout when one spouse keeps the house.
- Equalizing a property division with other assets or payments.
- Deciding whether to sell the home or keep it.
- Supporting a settlement proposal or a mediator's recommendation.
- One neutral appraiser hired by both spouses, with the valuation date and the photos agreed by both sides, so arguments about what happened to the house after the separation don't move the number.
- Values on more than one date, since California Family Code §2552 generally values community assets near the time of trial but lets the court choose another date for good cause.
Desktop suitability: Desktop appraisals work well for negotiation, mediation and agreed buyouts, where both sides mainly need an independent figure built from real sales. If the case is headed to trial and the other side may challenge every assumption, an inspection-based appraisal with expert testimony can be the stronger tool. Brian provides those through Brian Ward Appraisal.
Q: Can my spouse and I hire one appraiser together?
A: Yes, and many couples do. Both spouses can be named as joint clients, both attorneys can agree on the valuation date and on the photos the appraisal relies on, and the report states those agreed facts. If the house was neglected or damaged after the separation, a value as of the agreed date, built from photos taken then, keeps those later changes out of the number.
Q: How much is our house worth for the divorce?
A: That depends on the date your agreement or the court uses: often today, sometimes the date of separation, occasionally both. Tell us which date or dates when you order, and the report gives a value for each from sales around that time.
Q: My spouse lives in the house and won't let anyone in. Can you still appraise it?
A: Usually, yes. Public records, prior listing photos and your own knowledge of the home are often enough for a credible desktop appraisal, and the report states what it relied on.
Q: Can the appraisal be used in court?
A: Reports are prepared under USPAP and signed by a certified appraiser, and Brian has testified as an expert witness in family law matters. Whether a desktop report is the right exhibit for your hearing is a question for your attorney.

### Family Transfers & Co-Owner Buyouts
In plain English: When a house changes hands inside a family, an appraisal sets a fair price everyone can see and documents the deal for taxes later.
Selling the family home to one of the kids, buying a sibling out of an inherited house, or untangling a co-ownership between friends or partners: each of these deals goes more smoothly when everyone starts from the same independent value.
Agreements tend to form over a holiday weekend, before a relative flies home, or the day an attorney is ready to draft the paperwork. With 24-hour delivery the number arrives while everyone is still at the table.
- It gives co-owners a buyout figure nobody chose to suit themselves.
- It documents an arm's-length price if a sale below market value is later treated as part gift.
- It records the new owner's value for future tax and insurance questions.
- It turns a conversation about feelings into a conversation about sales.
Desktop suitability: Desktop appraisals suit family transactions well: the people who know the house best supply the information, and everyone can see exactly what the appraisal relied on. 
Q: How do I buy out my siblings' share of our parents' house?
A: Start with an independent appraisal so everyone works from the same value. Each share is usually figured from market value, less anything the family agrees to adjust for, and an attorney or escrow officer handles the paperwork.
Q: If I sell to my child below market value, do I need an appraisal?
A: The gap between fair market value and the price paid can count as a gift for federal gift-tax purposes, so many families document the value. Your tax advisor can tell you whether a gift-tax return is required.
Q: Can I use the appraisal to get a mortgage for the buyout?
A: No. Lenders order their own appraisals. A Cwift report is for pricing and documenting the transfer, not for loan underwriting.

### Gift Tax (Form 709)
In plain English: If you give a house, or part of one, to your children or into a trust, the IRS wants to know what it was worth that day. This appraisal is the proof that goes with the gift-tax return.
Transferring a house, or part of one, to a relative or into a trust? The gift's fair market value on the date of transfer belongs on the federal gift-tax return, and an appraisal from a qualified appraiser is the usual way to support it.
Form 709 is generally due by April 15 of the year after the gift, and planning moves such as deeding a share into a trust or closing a family sale before December 31 tend to pile up near deadlines. A 24-hour report keeps the return from waiting on the appraisal.
- Treasury regulations describe what an appraisal attached to a gift-tax return should contain: the dates, a description of the property, the appraisal process, assumptions and limiting conditions, the information considered, the methods, and the reasoning behind the value (Treas. Reg. §301.6501(c)-1(f)(3)).
- Adequate disclosure starts the IRS's three-year window to question the reported value; without it, that window can stay open.
- The regulation's appraiser requirements cover qualifications and independence, so the appraiser can't be the donor, the recipient or a family member.
- Gifts of a share in an LLC or family limited partnership that owns the house: the appraisal supplies the real estate value the entity valuation starts from.
Desktop suitability: The adequate-disclosure rules focus on the appraiser's qualifications and the contents of the report. They don't call for a physical inspection, and for most single-family and condominium gifts a desktop appraisal supplies what the return needs. Cwift values the property itself; if you are giving a fractional interest, any discount for a partial interest is a separate analysis, typically by a business valuation specialist. The same goes for a gift of an interest in an LLC or family limited partnership that holds real estate: the entity valuation usually starts from the market value of the property, and the specialist then applies any discounts for lack of control or lack of marketability. 
Q: Do I need an appraisal if the gift is small?
A: Most real estate gifts exceed the annual exclusion, but thresholds change. Your CPA or attorney can confirm whether a return is required and how the value should be supported.
Q: Can you appraise a gift that was made last year?
A: Yes. The appraisal is developed as of the transfer date, using sales from that period.
Q: Can you value a house owned by our family LLC or partnership?
A: Yes, the property itself. A business valuation specialist usually takes that value, adds the entity's other assets and debts, and applies any discounts for lack of control or marketability to the interest being given. Name the specialist as an intended user when you order.
Q: What about donating a house to a charity?
A: That's a charitable deduction with its own rules, not a Form 709 gift. Real estate donated for a deduction of more than $5,000 generally needs a qualified appraisal dated no earlier than 60 days before the donation, and the appraiser signs Form 8283, Section B. Tell us the donation date when you order, and you'll know before you pay whether a desktop report fits.

### Prop 19 Parent-Child Transfers
In plain English: When parents pass their home to a child, Prop 19 decides how much of the old, low property tax stays. The home's market value on the transfer date is the number that decides it.
Since February 16, 2021, Proposition 19 has narrowed California's parent-child property tax exclusion. A family home keeps part of its low assessment only when a child, or a qualifying grandchild, makes it their principal residence, and only up to a value cap. The home's market value on the transfer date tells you how much of the old assessment survives.
Move in, rent it out, sell it, or buy out siblings: each choice changes the tax bill, and families often have to decide quickly. The assessor's claim forms carry their own deadlines too.
- For transfers from February 16, 2025 through February 15, 2027, the exclusion covers the parent's factored base year value plus $1,044,586. Market value above that limit is added to the assessment (State Board of Equalization).
- Earlier windows used $1,000,000 (Feb 16, 2021 to Feb 15, 2023) and $1,022,600 (through Feb 15, 2025); the amount adjusts every two years.
- Parent-to-child transfers are claimed on form BOE-19-P with the county assessor; grandparent-to-grandchild transfers use BOE-19-G.
Desktop suitability: County assessors set values from sales data and records, generally without walking through the house. A desktop appraisal works from the same kind of evidence, examined property by property, which makes it a natural fit for Prop 19 planning and for questioning an assessor's figure. 
Q: Will my property taxes go up if I inherit my parents' house?
A: Often, yes. If you don't make it your main home, the county reassesses it at market value. If you move in and claim the exclusion, part of the old assessment can carry over, up to a cap. An appraisal of the home's value on the transfer date tells you which way it goes.
Q: Does the appraisal set my new property tax?
A: No. The county assessor sets the assessed value. The appraisal gives you an independent market value to plan with and, if needed, evidence for a review or appeal of the assessor's figure.
Q: What if the assessor's market value seems too high?
A: An independent appraisal of market value on the transfer date is the evidence you would bring to an informal review or a formal assessment appeal.

### Property Tax Appeals
In plain English: If you think the county values your home too high for property taxes, an independent appraisal is the evidence you bring to the assessor or the appeals board.
When a home's market value falls below its assessed value, Proposition 8 allows a temporary reduction. If the assessor won't agree, the county assessment appeals board hears the evidence, and an independent appraisal is the kind of evidence boards are used to weighing.
Regular appeal applications are filed between July 2 and either September 15 or November 30, depending on the county (State Board of Equalization). Appraisals ordered in the final days of the window are where 24-hour delivery earns its keep.
- Prop 8 decline-in-value requests to the assessor.
- Formal assessment appeals before the county board or a hearing officer.
- Questioning a base-year value set after a purchase, an inheritance or other change in ownership.
Desktop suitability: Appeals boards decide on evidence of market value, and a well-supported desktop appraisal presents the same comparable-sales evidence as an inspected one. If your county or hearing officer prefers a particular report format, ask before you order.
Q: How do I lower my property taxes in California?
A: If your home's market value on January 1 was below its assessed value, ask the county assessor for a Prop 8 decline-in-value review. If that doesn't work, file an appeal with the county board during the filing period. An independent appraisal of the January 1 value is the evidence.
Q: Will an appraisal guarantee a lower assessment?
A: No one can promise that. The appraisal provides independent evidence of market value, which the board weighs against the assessor's evidence.
Q: Which date should the appraisal use?
A: For a decline-in-value appeal, January 1 of the tax year in question, the lien date. Tell us the year and the effective date is set to match.

### Bankruptcy
In plain English: A bankruptcy filing has to list what your house is worth. Your attorney uses this appraisal for that number and to show how much equity the homestead exemption protects.
Bankruptcy schedules ask for the current value of the debtor's real estate, and that number ripples through the whole case: how much equity the homestead exemption protects, what a Chapter 7 trustee might pursue, and what a Chapter 13 plan has to pay unsecured creditors.
A foreclosure sale date, a wage garnishment or a meeting of creditors can compress the timeline. When counsel needs the value before the petition goes out, a 24-hour appraisal fits the schedule.
- Real property values on Schedule A/B.
- Equity and homestead exemption analysis under California's rules.
- Chapter 13 plan feasibility and the liquidation comparison.
- Responding when a trustee or creditor proposes a different value.
Desktop suitability: Desktop appraisals are widely used to set schedule values and plan a case. Photos, contractor bids and descriptions of defects all feed into the condition rating and the comparable adjustments. If the trustee or a creditor contests value, your attorney may want an inspection-based appraisal and expert testimony, which Brian also provides through Brian Ward Appraisal.
Q: How much is my house worth for bankruptcy?
A: Its fair market value as of the date your attorney specifies, usually the petition date. The appraisal reports that value with the comparable sales behind it, and photos of needed repairs count.
Q: Should the value be as of the filing date?
A: Schedules generally use value as of the petition date, and your attorney will specify. A past date is no problem; retrospective appraisals are routine.
Q: Can a desktop appraisal account for needed repairs?
A: Yes. Send photos of the problems along with any bids or estimates, and they are reflected in the analysis.

### Pre-Listing Pricing
In plain English: Before you put a house on the market, find out what it's really worth from someone who isn't trying to win the listing.
An agent's suggested list price is a marketing opinion. An appraisal is an independent opinion of market value from someone with nothing riding on the sale. Trustees, executors and owners selling without an agent use a pre-listing appraisal to anchor the price and to answer the buyer's appraiser later.
The photographer is booked, the agent is ready and the market moves weekly. A 24-hour appraisal lets you settle the price before the listing goes live instead of cutting it after the home sits.
- A list price backed by recent comparable sales.
- A neutral check on competing agents' pricing opinions.
- Trust and estate sales, where the fiduciary should be able to show the price was reasonable.
- Sales data in hand before the buyer's lender appraisal comes back.
Desktop suitability: Pricing doesn't require an inspection; it requires good comparables and an honest read of the market, which is exactly what a desktop appraisal delivers. 
Q: How much is my house worth before I sell it?
A: A pre-listing appraisal answers that with recent comparable sales and an independent opinion of market value, emailed within 24 hours of payment and photos.
Q: Will the buyer's lender accept my appraisal?
A: No. The buyer's lender orders its own appraisal. Yours helps you set a supportable price and gives you sales data to discuss if that appraisal comes in low.
Q: Can you value the home as if planned repairs were done?
A: Often, yes. Describe the repairs when you order and you'll get an answer before you're invoiced.

### Pre-Purchase Value Check
In plain English: Before you buy, especially with cash or from family, check whether the price makes sense while you can still back out.
Buyers paying cash, buying from family, or competing without an appraisal contingency still want to know whether the price makes sense. A pre-purchase desktop appraisal gives you an independent opinion of market value while you can still negotiate or walk away.
California purchase contracts give buyers a limited window to investigate and remove contingencies. A report delivered within 24 hours fits inside that window with room to act on it.
- Cash buyers who won't have a lender's appraisal.
- Buyers who waived the appraisal contingency to win the offer.
- Off-market and family purchases with no listing history to lean on.
- Anyone who wants a second opinion on a price they've been quoted.
Desktop suitability: Buyers rarely spend more than a showing inside a house before the contingency clock runs out. A desktop appraisal works from listing photos, disclosures and your observations, plus the same market analysis any appraisal uses. 
Q: Should I get my own appraisal before buying a house?
A: If you're buying with cash, from a relative or without an appraisal contingency, an independent appraisal is a sensible check on the price while you can still negotiate or walk away.
Q: Can I use this appraisal for my mortgage?
A: No. Your lender must order its own appraisal under appraiser-independence rules. This report is for your own decision.
Q: What about a duplex or vacant land?
A: Cwift appraises single-family homes and condominiums only. For other property types, contact Brian Ward Appraisal.

### Immigration Sponsors (Form I-864)
In plain English: If you're sponsoring a relative and your income falls short on paper, the equity in your home can count. Immigration officials want a recent appraisal to prove its value.
A sponsor whose income falls short of the I-864 requirement can count assets, and the equity in a home can be one of them. The I-864 instructions define a home's net value as its appraised value minus every loan secured by it, and they ask sponsors who use it to include a recent appraisal by a licensed appraiser.
Requests for evidence from the National Visa Center or USCIS carry response dates, and one missing document can hold up an entire case. A 24-hour appraisal clears that item quickly.
- Proof of ownership, such as the deed.
- A recent appraisal by a licensed appraiser establishing the home's value.
- Statements for every mortgage or lien, so net equity can be calculated.
- Assets count only if they can be converted to cash within one year without considerable hardship, and officers decide how much weight real estate deserves.
Desktop suitability: The I-864 instructions ask for a recent appraisal by a licensed appraiser; they don't specify an inspection. A desktop appraisal from a California Certified Residential appraiser documents value quickly and clearly. Your immigration attorney can advise whether relying on home equity makes sense in your case.
Q: How recent does the appraisal need to be?
A: The instructions ask for a recent appraisal, so order close to the date you'll submit the evidence.
Q: Can I use the home I live in?
A: The I-864 instructions allow sponsors to include the net value of their home as an asset, subject to the rules on assets. Your attorney can confirm how they apply to you.

### Bail & Property Bonds
In plain English: To use a house instead of cash for bail, the court needs proof that the owner's equity is at least twice the bail. A current appraisal is that proof.
California lets a property owner post real estate equity instead of cash bail under Penal Code §1298, but the court must find that the equity is at least twice the bail amount. That finding starts with a current appraisal.
When the appraisal is the last document missing from the property-bond packet, 24-hour delivery gets the packet to the clerk sooner.
- Superior courts publish their own property-bond instructions, and many call for an appraisal by a California-licensed or certified appraiser with the license number on the report.
- Some courts require the appraisal to be recent, for example within the last six months, and some specify a report form.
- Bail agents who accept real estate as collateral often want an appraisal to confirm the equity.
Desktop suitability: Many courts accept an appraisal without specifying an inspection, but requirements vary by county. Check your court's packet or ask your bail agent before ordering. If an inspected appraisal is required, Brian Ward Appraisal provides them in San Diego and Riverside Counties.
Q: Can I use my house for bail in California?
A: Often, yes. Under Penal Code §1298 a court can accept equity in real estate instead of cash if the equity is at least twice the bail amount. Each court sets its own paperwork, and a current appraisal is usually part of it.
Q: Does the equity need to be twice the bail?
A: Under Penal Code §1298 the court must find that the equity is at least twice the bail amount. Equity is the appraised value minus the loans and liens against the property.
Q: Do bail agents accept property as collateral?
A: Many do. Ask the agent which report and effective date they need before you order.


## Credibility brief

### The standards don't require a site visit
USPAP, published by the Appraisal Standards Board of The Appraisal Foundation, is the set of standards appraisers follow throughout the United States, and California law requires licensed appraisers to comply with it. The current edition took effect on January 1, 2024, and has no end date.
Its Scope of Work Rule makes the appraiser responsible for deciding what research and analysis are needed to produce credible results for the intended use. Advisory Opinion 2 treats the extent of any inspection as part of that scope of work, which can vary with the assignment. What USPAP does require is disclosure: the certification must state whether the appraiser personally inspected the property, and the report must describe the information relied on.

### Lenders already rely on desktop appraisals
Fannie Mae's Selling Guide (B4-1.2-02) describes desktop appraisals reported on Form 1004 Desktop, whose minimum scope of work does not require a current inspection of the property or the comparable sales. The appraiser relies on data from other sources. They are eligible for certain one-unit, principal-residence purchase loans with loan-to-value ratios of 90% or less.
Freddie Mac accepts desktop appraisals for eligible purchase transactions as well. If the companies that back home mortgages accept desktop appraisals for loans secured by the house, the method is credible for the estate, tax and family decisions on this site.

### Tax rules focus on who signs and what the report says
For gift-tax returns, Treasury regulations describe an appraisal that satisfies adequate disclosure (26 CFR §301.6501(c)-1(f)(3)). The appraiser must regularly perform appraisals, be qualified for the type of property, and be independent of the donor and the recipient. The report must state the dates and purpose, describe the property and the appraisal process, list assumptions and limiting conditions, identify the information considered, and explain the procedures, the method and the specific basis for the value. None of those requirements is a physical inspection.
For inherited property, the heir's basis is generally the fair market value at the date of death (IRC §1014). The appraisal is the documentation of that value, and its credibility rests on the appraiser's qualifications and the quality of the analysis.

### Comparable sales have always been studied remotely
In any appraisal, inspected or not, the appraiser does not tour the comparable sales. Their features and condition come from MLS records, listing photographs, public records and market data. Most of the evidence behind any value opinion is gathered this way. A desktop appraisal applies the same research method to the subject property.

### The owner's evidence is often better than a short visit
Photographs of every room, measurements, permits, invoices and the owner's account of repairs can document a home more completely than a brief walk-through, especially for the work nobody can see. When information turns out to be wrong, the remedy is built in: Cwift revises the appraisal at no charge if the home's features, quality or condition were misread or misdescribed.

### Past dates can't be inspected anyway
Date-of-death, gift, separation and transfer appraisals value a home as it was on an earlier date. A visit today would document today's condition, after a clean-out, repairs or a remodel. The credible approach, in any format, is to reconstruct the earlier condition from evidence and to rely on sales from that period.

### The appraiser is fully accountable
Every Cwift report is signed by Brian Ward, California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser, license AR036053, issued by the California Bureau of Real Estate Appraisers (BREA), which licenses and disciplines appraisers. The license can be verified with BREA's public appraiser search. USPAP requires the appraiser to keep a workfile supporting each report for at least five years, and longer when testimony is involved, so the analysis can be examined if the value is ever questioned.

Sources:
- The Appraisal Foundation, Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP), 2024 edition: https://www.appraisalfoundation.org/imis/TAF/Standards/Appraisal_Standards/Uniform_Standards_of_Professional_Appraisal_Practice/TAF/USPAP.aspx
- Fannie Mae Selling Guide B4-1.2-02, Desktop Appraisals: https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b4-1.2-02/desktop-appraisals
- Freddie Mac Single-Family Seller/Servicer Guide, Section 5604.1 (desktop appraisals): https://guide.freddiemac.com/app/guide/section/5604.1
- 26 CFR §301.6501(c)-1(f)(3), adequate disclosure of gifts (appraisal requirements): https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-26/chapter-I/subchapter-F/part-301/subpart-ECFR47464f8a81aa5b0/subject-group-ECFR2b9daa72e34967f/section-301.6501(c)-1
- California Bureau of Real Estate Appraisers (BREA), license search: https://www.brea.ca.gov/

## Area pages

### Alameda County (https://www.cwift.com/california/alameda-county)
Certified desktop appraisals for Alameda County homes, delivered within 24 hours of photos and payment.
County seat: Oakland. 2026 regular assessment-appeal filing deadline: September 15. Probate cases for Alameda County estates are heard in the Superior Court of California, County of Alameda, and Oakland is the county seat. Prop 19 parent-child claims and Prop 8 decline-in-value reviews go to the Alameda County Assessor. Alameda County's 2026 regular assessment-appeal filing period ran from July 2 to September 15. Each of these looks at value on a set date, such as a date of death, a transfer or January 1, and a Cwift report can be written to any of them.
ZIP codes: 49 ZIP codes
Across Alameda County, from Oakland and Piedmont to Castro Valley and Livermore, many houses have stayed with one owner for decades. When that owner dies, heirs need a date of death value for stepped-up basis, trustees need a figure before dividing shares, and a child thinking about moving into a San Leandro house faces a Prop 19 decision. Divorce brings the same need when one spouse keeps a Pleasanton or Dublin home, and Tri-Valley owners who bought near a market peak may want a Prop 8 review.
Alameda County housing runs from Victorian cottages on the island city of Alameda and in West Oakland to brown-shingle and Craftsman homes in Rockridge and Temescal. Postwar ranch tracts fill San Leandro, San Lorenzo, Castro Valley and Union City, while the Oakland hills hold mid-century houses and homes rebuilt after the 1991 firestorm on steep, wooded lots. Over the hills, Pleasanton, Dublin and Livermore grew with postwar and later subdivisions, including Dublin Ranch and other master-planned neighborhoods with HOAs. Condos cluster near BART stations and along the Oakland and Emeryville waterfronts.
- Homes in the Hayward Fault's mapped earthquake zones, from Fremont to Berkeley, carry seller disclosures; foundation bolting or retrofit work shown in photos and permits is weighed against matching sales.
- Hill homes above Oakland and Berkeley sit in high fire hazard zones, where roof material, brush clearance and insurance availability affect buyers, so clear exterior and lot photos shape the condition rating.
- Newer subdivisions in Dublin and other Tri-Valley areas can carry Mello-Roos special taxes and HOA dues; the appraisal reads both from tax and association records and compares homes with similar yearly charges.
Places: Oakland, Alameda, San Leandro, Castro Valley, Pleasanton, Livermore, Dublin, Piedmont
Q: Can an appraisal show my Alameda County home lost value for property taxes?
A: Yes. A Prop 8 decline-in-value review compares a home's assessed value with its market value on January 1, so the appraisal is dated to that lien date and relies on sales from around it. The report can support an informal review request to the Alameda County Assessor or a formal appeal in the next filing window. The assessor or appeals board decides, so no reduction is promised.

### Alpine County (https://www.cwift.com/california/alpine-county)
Certified home appraisals for Alpine County cabins and mountain homes, emailed within 24 hours.
County seat: Markleeville. 2026 regular assessment-appeal filing deadline: September 15. Probate for an Alpine County estate is handled by the Superior Court of California, County of Alpine, and Markleeville is the county seat. Prop 19 parent-child claims and Prop 8 decline-in-value reviews go to the Alpine County Assessor. Alpine County's 2026 regular assessment-appeal filing period ran from July 2 to September 15. Because an Alpine County cabin can sit empty for months, an appraisal for any of these purposes names its effective date and the condition it assumes on that day.
ZIP codes: 96120
Alpine County has only a handful of towns, and many cabins in Markleeville, Woodfords and Bear Valley have been weekend places for decades. When a parent dies, heirs who live in the valley or out of state need to know what the house is worth before they keep it, sell it or buy out a sibling. Winter complicates the timing, with Ebbetts and Monitor passes closed for months and the drive over Carson Pass slow in storms. A 24-hour desktop appraisal from Cwift works from photos, Alpine County records and nearby mountain sales, so an inherited house does not have to wait for spring.
Most of Alpine County is national forest and wilderness, so private land is scarce and homes cluster in a few spots. Markleeville has older wood-frame houses and cabins along Markleeville Creek and the East Fork of the Carson River. Woodfords, Mesa Vista, Paynesville and Fredericksburg sit at the edge of the Carson Valley on larger parcels among sagebrush and Jeffrey pines. Bear Valley, at the end of the plowed stretch of Highway 4, is a village of ski condos, chalets and A-frames built from the late 1960s on, and Kirkwood straddles the county line with condos and newer mountain homes.
- Seasonal access: cabins reached by unplowed roads, or only by snowmobile in winter, sell to fewer buyers, so the appraisal compares them with sales that share the same limits.
- Wildfire: the 2021 Tamarack Fire forced evacuations around Markleeville and Woodfords, so burned slopes, defensible space and any rebuilt structures are noted from photos and records.
- Condo HOAs at Kirkwood and Bear Valley carry dues, snow-removal costs and rental rules, and the appraiser reads those documents and leans on sales within the same complex.
Places: Markleeville, Woodfords, Mesa Vista, Alpine Village, Paynesville, Fredericksburg, Bear Valley, Kirkwood
Q: Can my late uncle's Alpine County cabin be appraised while the pass is snowed in?
A: Yes. The appraisal is built from interior and exterior photos, county records and sales around Markleeville, Bear Valley and Kirkwood, so no appraiser has to make the drive. If nobody can reach the cabin until spring, recent photos already on hand may work, and the report states plainly what it assumes about condition on the effective date.

In Amador County, houses from the Victorians above Sutter Creek's Main Street to the ranch parcels of the Shenandoah Valley tend to stay with one owner for decades, so a certified value usually comes up at a death, a trust or a divorce. Q: If I move into my mom's Amador County house, does Prop 19 need an appraisal?

A certified appraisal dated to the transfer gives the Amador County Assessor a supported figure to review. A tax professional can explain how the result applies to a specific situation.

### Butte County (https://www.cwift.com/california/butte-county)
Certified Butte County home appraisals in 24 hours, from Chico and Oroville to the Ridge.
County seat: Oroville. 2026 regular assessment-appeal filing deadline: November 30. When a Butte County estate goes through probate, the case is heard in the Superior Court of California, County of Butte, and the date-of-death value of a Chico or Oroville house is often the largest figure in the inventory. Prop 19 parent-child claims and Prop 8 decline-in-value reviews are made to the Butte County Assessor. Butte County's 2026 regular assessment-appeal filing period was set for July 2 to November 30.
ZIP codes: 16 ZIP codes
In Butte County, the need for a certified home value usually follows a death, a divorce or a fire. Many houses in Chico's older neighborhoods and around Oroville have had one owner for decades, so an inherited house brings a step-up in basis and Prop 19 choices at the same time. In Magalia, Concow and across the Camp Fire burn area, many owners now hold homes rebuilt since 2018, and a sale, a buyout or a trust split needs a value that reflects the new construction. Butte County climbs from flat rice and orchard country on the valley floor through oak foothills to pine-covered ridges. On the Ridge east of Chico, new site-built and manufactured homes stand beside lots not yet rebuilt after the Camp Fire.
- On the Ridge and in Concow, the report notes whether a home predates the Camp Fire or was rebuilt after it, and compares it with sales of similar post-fire construction.
- In the foothills and on the Ridge, costly or hard-to-find fire coverage can thin the pool of buyers, and recent nearby sales show that effect better than any rule of thumb.
- Homes along the Feather River below Oroville and near Gridley can sit in mapped flood areas, and the report notes the zone from public flood maps.
Places: Chico, Oroville, Paradise, Magalia, Gridley, Biggs, Durham, Thermalito
Q: Our Butte County house was rebuilt after the Camp Fire. How do appraisers value it?

Q: How is a Mammoth Lakes condo valued for an estate in Mono County?
A: Mostly against sales in the same complex or very similar ones nearby, as of the date of death. Places: Yreka, Mount Shasta, Weed, Dunsmuir, McCloud, Etna, Fort Jones, Tulelake

A: Yes. A desktop appraisal does not require anyone to reach the cabin now. Corona's oldest homes sit inside Grand Boulevard, the mile-wide circle around downtown, where Victorians, Craftsman bungalows and Spanish-style houses from the 1920s share streets with postwar infill. Ranch tracts from the 1950s and 1960s surround that core. Hillside areas such as Sierra del Oro have view lots, and the foothills of the Santa Ana Mountains rise to the south.
- Homes inside the Grand Boulevard circle range from carefully restored to heavily altered. Photos of original windows, floors and trim, plus permit history, help place a house against the right sales.
- Some South Corona tracts carry Mello-Roos taxes and HOA dues on top of the base property tax. The appraisal reads both and compares homes with similar ongoing costs.
- Hillside lots along the Santa Ana Mountains face wildfire exposure that can affect insurance and buyer demand. Fire hazard maps and photos of brush clearance are part of the review.
- Freeway frontage along the 91 and 15, and golf-course or view lots in Eagle Glen and Dos Lagos, can move value in opposite directions. Aerial images and owner photos show which applies.

Q: We're divorcing and I want to keep our Corona house, what's a fair buyout?

Much of Highland Park lies inside the Highland Park-Garvanza historic preservation overlay zone, a large district of early 1900s Craftsman bungalows and Victorian houses, many on terraced lots with arroyo-stone walls and porches. Mount Washington rises to the west on winding, narrow roads, with hillside cottages, 1950s post-and-beam houses and modern homes on steep lots, many looking toward downtown or the San Gabriel Mountains. Glassell Park and Cypress Park add 1920s bungalows and Spanish cottages, and Hermon borders Debs Park.
- Preservation-zone rules: exterior work in the Highland Park-Garvanza zone needs city review, so original windows, siding and porches matter, and permitted restorations are weighed against similar restored sales.
- Mount Washington access: narrow, winding roads, limited parking and steep driveways shape value, and the appraiser checks street width and slope from maps and photos when picking comparables.
- Views from the hills: Mount Washington lots facing downtown, the San Gabriel Mountains or the Arroyo Seco sell above enclosed lots, and the appraiser confirms the view from photos and aerial imagery.
- Arroyo-stone walls and foundations: terraced lots built with river rock can need costly structural work, and visible cracks or leaning walls are noted from photos and reflected in the condition rating.
Places: Garvanza, Hermon, Glassell Park, Cypress Park, Sycamore Grove, York Boulevard, Figueroa Street, Elyria Canyon Park
Q: How does an appraiser value a fixer Craftsman in Highland Park from photos?
A: By matching condition, not just size. The appraiser studies your photos of the foundation, roof, electrical panel, kitchen and baths, then compares the house with Highland Park sales of other unrenovated homes rather than flipped ones. Obvious problems such as cracked foundations or old knob-and-tube wiring are noted. A contractor's bid, if you have one, helps explain the condition rating.

Divorcing owners need a number for the house one spouse keeps, and others want to know what the house is worth before selling or questioning their property taxes. Cwift completes the appraisal from photos, records and Indio sales.
Indio's older neighborhoods near downtown and along Highway 111 have small stucco homes from the 1940s through the 1960s on flat lots with mature palms. Q: Can I keep my dad's low property tax on his Indio house under Prop 19?
A: Possibly. Under Prop 19, a child who moves into an inherited family home as a primary residence can keep part or all of the parent's assessed value, but a cap tied to the home's market value on the transfer date applies. That makes the date-of-death value important. Cwift provides the appraisal, the Riverside County Assessor decides the claim, and a tax advisor can explain the details.

A: Sometimes. If the market value on January 1 was below the assessed value on your tax bill, Prop 8 lets the Riverside County Assessor lower it temporarily. An appraisal built on Mission Grove sales from around that date gives solid support for an informal review or a formal appeal. The assessor or appeals board makes the decision, and no appraisal can promise a reduction.

Q: Is my late aunt's Laguna Woods co-op appraised differently from a condo?
A: Yes. A co-op in Laguna Woods Village is a membership in a mutual rather than a deeded unit, so it is compared with recent co-op sales, while condominium manors are compared with condo sales. - Many postwar Ontario houses gained a bedroom or den in the garage; the report checks permit records, since permitted and unpermitted conversions are valued differently.

Q: Does my Ontario house need an appraisal for a Chapter 13 bankruptcy filing?
A: Many bankruptcy attorneys ask for one. Cwift values the house as of the filing date or another date the attorney names, using photos, records and Ontario sales, and the attorney decides how the report is used.

Pacific Beach and Mission Beach hold beach cottages and bayfront homes that some owners have kept since the 1950s and 1960s. When one of those owners dies, the heirs have big decisions to make quickly. Divorcing owners of a Crown Point house or a condo near Garnet Avenue need a neutral figure too. Cwift provides it in a 24-hour desktop appraisal.
Pacific Beach mixes 1920s to 1950s beach cottages and bungalows with 1960s and 1970s apartments, condos and newer two- and three-story homes on small lots. Q: Our parents bought their Pacific Beach cottage decades ago. How does the step-up in basis work?
A: In general, an heir's tax basis resets to what the property was worth when the owner died, which can sharply reduce capital gains when the heirs later sell. A date-of-death appraisal of the Pacific Beach cottage documents that value. For a married couple's community property, special rules can apply when the first spouse dies, so a CPA should confirm the details.

Washington Square and Wilshire Square mix Craftsman bungalows and period revival houses, and Park Santiago adds homes along Santiago Creek. Downtown adds lofts and condos near the Artists Village. Beyond the older core, 1950s and 1960s ranch tracts cover much of the city, with converted garages, small duplexes and condo complexes mixed in.
- Floral Park and French Park homes are judged on preserved period details, so a restored house is compared with similar intact homes, and any Mills Act contract is noted.
- Converted garages, rear units and room additions are common in Santa Ana's postwar tracts, and permit history separates legal living area from space buyers would discount.
- Large-lot streets in Floral Park and along Santiago Creek carry land value beyond the house, measured with parcel maps and nearby sales.
- Nearness to the 5 freeway, Bristol Street or busy downtown blocks can change value street by street, so comparables come from similar settings.
Places: Floral Park, French Park, Washington Square, Wilshire Square, Park Santiago, Downtown Santa Ana, Artists Village, Santiago Creek
Q: Do I need a home appraisal in Santa Ana for a Chapter 7 bankruptcy?
A: Often, yes. The bankruptcy schedules ask for the home's current value, and trustees in the Santa Ana Division look closely at whether equity exceeds the homestead exemption. A desktop appraisal gives a supportable value from photos, county records and recent Santa Ana sales, emailed within 24 hours. A bankruptcy attorney decides how to use it and which exemption applies.

Q: Does Mello-Roos on my Santa Clarita house lower what it appraises for?

Q: Our family trust holds a Santa Monica house; what appraisal does the trustee need?

Q: How is a South LA lot with a front house and a back house appraised?
A: First the appraiser confirms what the back house legally is, using city permits and county records: a permitted ADU, an older legal second unit or an unpermitted structure. The Sunset District's rows of stucco houses were mostly built from the 1920s through the 1940s, and many have been owned for decades. Many of these homes are still full of furniture when the estate starts, and the value has to be set without waiting for a cleanout.

Q: Can Grandma's Sunset District house be appraised while it's still full of furniture?
A: Yes. Photos do not need to be staged; they need to show each room clearly, along with the kitchen, baths, windows, garage and exterior. The appraiser rates finishes, layout and condition, not furnishings, and compares the house with Sunset sales of similar row houses. Many estates order the appraisal first and clear the house later, since the value is tied to the date of death anyway.

Q: Does Mello-Roos lower what my Temecula house is worth in an appraisal?
A: It can. Buyers look at the total yearly tax bill, so two similar houses can sell differently if one carries a larger Mello-Roos tax or has more years left on it. Mooney Grove Park, with one of the largest valley oak groves in California, sits at the south end of Mooney Boulevard, and east of town, ranchettes and acreage homes sit among walnut and citrus orchards toward the Kaweah Oaks Preserve.
- Older homes near Mill Creek and downtown Visalia range from carefully restored to original. Photos of the roof, foundation, wiring and kitchen show where a house falls among Visalia's older-home sales.
- Pools, owned solar and central air matter through Visalia's long, hot summers. Photos of the equipment and permit records show what is there, and Visalia sales show what buyers pay for it.
- Ranchettes east of Visalia often have wells, septic systems and outbuildings. Records and photos document each, and the comparables come from similar Tulare County rural homes rather than city tracts.
- Newer Visalia subdivisions may carry landscape and lighting assessments. The tax bill is checked, and sales inside the same Visalia subdivision guide the value.
Places: Downtown Visalia, Mill Creek, Mooney Boulevard, Mooney Grove Park, North Visalia, Southwest Visalia, Green Acres
Q: Can I get my own appraisal before making an offer on a Visalia house?
A: Yes. Pricing a purchase is one of the uses Cwift covers. With photos from the listing or the seller's agent, Tulare County records and recent Visalia sales, the report gives an independent value within 24 hours of payment and photos, often in time to shape an offer. Q: Do the barn and arena on my Yucaipa horse property add to its appraised value?
